items.title: AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The vocabulary of AI coding, translated into plain English for engineers.

items.title: AI | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: A moving label, not a technology. Points at whatever computers can newly, impressively do — right now, large language models.

items.title: Model | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The parameters. Stateless — does next-token prediction and nothing else. Cannot do anything agentic on its own.

items.title: Parameters | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The numbers inside a model — often billions — tuned during training. Everything the model knows lives in them. Also called weights.

items.title: Training | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The process that sets a model's parameters by exposing it to vast amounts of text and adjusting to improve next-token prediction.

items.title: Inference | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Running a trained model to generate output — what happens on every model provider request. Parameters stay fixed.

items.title: Effort | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: A dial for how much reasoning the model does before it answers. More effort spends more output tokens for a better shot at hard problems.

items.title: Token | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The atomic unit a model reads and writes. Roughly word-sized but not exactly. Context window size, cost, and latency all count tokens.

items.title: Next-token prediction | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: What the model actually does. Samples one next token from the context, appends it, and runs again. Its only mode of operation.

items.title: Non-determinism | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The same input can produce different output. A property of how models generate text and how providers serve requests.

items.title: Model provider | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Whatever serves a model for inference. Usually remote (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google), but can also be local (Ollama, llama.cpp).

items.title: Harness | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Everything around the model that turns it into an agent: tools, system prompt, context-window management, permissions, hooks.

items.title: Model provider request | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: One round-trip from the harness to the model provider. The harness sends context; the provider returns one response.

items.title: Input tokens | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Tokens the harness sends on each model provider request. Billed at a lower rate than output tokens.

items.title: Output tokens | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Tokens the model generates back. Billed at a higher rate than input tokens, since they cost more compute to produce.

items.title: Prefix cache | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The provider-side store that lets consecutive requests skip re-processing a shared prefix, billing those tokens at a lower rate.

items.title: Cache tokens | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Input tokens the provider has cached from a previous request via its prefix cache, billed at a much lower rate.

items.title: Stateless | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Carries no information forward. The model is stateless across requests; an agent is stateless across sessions by default.

items.title: Context | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: The relevant information the agent has access to right now — what the agent knows that's pertinent to the task.

items.title: Context window | AI Coding Dictionary
items.summary: Everything the model sees on each model provider request. Finite, model-specific, the only surface through which the model perceives.
